about: The machine: every state, edge, rule, said-line and law of shroom v1 — the spec (DECISIONS B133). Sessions edit it; MACHINE.md and the canvas's machine boards are generated from it.
notation: States are kebab-case, stable, scaffold-grade names; events are written in bold, [guards] in brackets, and said-lines in quotes. Every region carries its failure classification and resume semantics — the POC's wizard discipline generalized: attempt → classify → route to the fix → auto-poll → resume (POC §6) — and state is derived from probes, never stored as a step counter (UX-STATEMACHINE.md L92-98). Status keys used across the fixture: the ledger's When column carries a date for ratified rows and “· autonomous — awaiting ratification” for N29–N42 (designed 2026-09-30, L22-29); in the inventory R = ratified by Bagrat and D = designed in the autonomous sitting, awaiting ratification (= provisional), with faces that are row facts or copy variants folded into their state per N18 (L1666-1669); said-lines are drafts unless their section is marked copy ratified (L6-9). Fixture provenance: ledger entries are the table rows at L38-90 in table order (P17 at L38 … N42 at L90; N17 sits after N19), title = the Question cell and decision = the Decision cell, both verbatim markdown source; law rules are the markdown source with line wraps joined by single spaces; inventory entries are rows L1673-1709 in order, states split on top-level “ · ” with backticks dropped (non-scaffold descriptive faces kept verbatim, e.g. “source view”, “delete sheet”, “Add another Mac”), status given as “normalized | verbatim cell”; surfaces are rows L1715-1720 with may_do = the Lives | Opens | Rules cells joined by “ | ”; absent-list items (L1724-1734, split on “ · ”) and scaffold flags (L1740-1762, markdown source) each carry a two-space-separated [Lnnn] source suffix; amends/amended_by entries are “ID (relation)” strings covering every explicit amends / amended / refined / reversed / replaces / extends / settles / resolves marker in the ledger, recorded on both sides (non-ledger targets such as “Region 4 beat 6” kept as text). Spec observations for the test author: N31 says it replaces “the merged expired/used row (N18)”, but N18's ledger roster as written lists no such row (the only other mention is the N31 section heading, L1530); P1, P5, P8, P11, P13 (absent list) and P12 (N33) are cited but have no row in this ledger (only P17 does); the state inventory carries no row for countdown's or config's sub-faces beyond those listed, and “stopping” (R) has no ledger citation.

events.about: How a rule names the events it moves on. A pattern is an event's kind as the core's `Event` names it: `TrayClicked`, `WindowClosed`, `Act(Restart)`, `Cloud(Swept)`, `Failed(Wire)`; a bare `Cloud`, `Rec`, `Os` or `Failed` matches every kind under it. The words below stand for several.

laws.title: State is derived, never a step counter
laws.rule: **State is derived, never a step counter** — every entry re-probes reality (POC §6/§8, Region 2's backbone). A face clears by itself when its cause does (N34).
invariants: Persisted state under ~/.shroom holds no wizard step counter or step index; the current state id is a pure function of probe results: derive(probes) called twice with identical probes returns the identical state id.
Every entry (launch, relaunch, reconnect, window reopen, tray click) runs the probes before choosing a state; no transition target is read from a stored 'last step'.

Kill + relaunch in any state S lands in derive(probes), not in S by memory — e.g. a relaunch mid account-signing-up re-enters at the virgin fork (N19); wizard-offline on reconnect routes by derived state (N18).
Every derived face (member-revoked, space-needs-owner, space-gone, space-degraded, recording-off) disappears with no user action once its cause probe clears.

laws.title: The recording is sacred
laws.rule: **The recording is sacred** — capture is local whatever the network or the space does; a crash leaves a saved take (N25); a full disk finalizes (N39); a space that went away leaves Save to Movies (N34). Nothing shroom does ever loses a take the user didn't discard.
invariants: No network, space, or upload failure event causes a transition out of recording or paused; capture bytes keep landing locally whatever those probes say.

Local take bytes are removed only by an explicit user act — discard-confirm → Discard, the saved-take banner's Discard… confirmed, or Restart (whose old take dies only when the new capture begins, N39); no crash, disk-full, auto-pause, offline, or space-loss transition deletes them.
After a simulated crash mid-take, the next launch has the take saved and the recovered-take banner present in config with the amber tray face.
A full disk mid-take enters disk-full-stop with the take finalized, never discarded or auto-published; left unanswered it remains a saved take (disk_full_stop → recovered_take, L898).
When a take can't reach the space (stopped-stranded, member-revoked, space-gone), Save to Movies is offered; it copies the single file to ~/Movies and the take keeps waiting until discarded (N34).

laws.title: Only you make a link
laws.rule: **Only you make a link** — a link comes into being by Finish & Share (the stop) or Get link, never by a crash, a full disk, or an auto-pause (N25, N39). Stop = published (§5.3) — the one place that's said is the paused popover's “Finish & Share”, by its name (B143: it was Stop, with a quiet line beneath).
invariants: A link/page id comes into being only on Stop or Get link events; crash recovery, disk-full-stop, and every auto-pause (display-lost, mic-lost, camera-lost, mac-away, permission-lost) create no link and open no page.
disk-full-stop and a lost screen grant finalize and ask; neither transitions to a page-open or upload-published state without a user Stop/Get link.
No surface says “Your link opens right away.”: Bagrat took the quiet line off the paused popover's stop, now “Finish & Share” (B143), so it reads like the rows beside it.

laws.title: The quiet-take law
laws.rule: **The quiet-take law** *(N41)* — while a take is open (recording *or* paused), shroom puts nothing new on screen: invites, deep links, windows, the deferred page of an offline stop, update banners — all wait for the take to end. Only the bubble and macOS's own indicator can ever appear in a take (the agent label and the marker toast show to the person only, left out of the recording — N62, N78); the paused popover exists only after the pause is confirmed (POC §8). **And nothing that would end, move or replace the app runs mid-take** — Update, Disconnect, Leave, joining another space, Quit (⌘Q or the Dock, reachable when a window was already open) — their buttons grey with “You can do this once your recording is finished.”; a Quit request is declined silently while recording and opens the paused popover (its “no Quit while a take is open” note) while paused.
invariants: Let take_open = state ∈ {recording, paused, and paused's morphs/auto-pause faces}. While take_open, no window, banner, invite, deep-link handling, deferred offline-stop page, or update banner becomes newly visible; the only shroom surfaces that may newly appear are the bubble overlay, the paused popover (only after the pause is confirmed) and its morphs (discard-confirm), and the auto-pause popovers (display-lost, mic-lost, camera-lost, mac-away, permission-lost, disk-full-stop); and, left out of every capture, the agent label (N62) and the marker toast for two seconds after ⌥⌘M (N78).
Items that arrive while take_open (invite deep link, offline-stop page, update banner, windows) are queued and surface only after the take ends.
While take_open, Update, Disconnect, Leave, join-another-space and Quit controls are disabled and show “You can do this once your recording is finished.”

A Quit request (⌘Q or Dock) while recording causes no state change and no visible surface; while paused it opens/keeps the paused popover showing its “no Quit while a take is open” note; the process keeps running in both.
The paused popover is never visible before the capture engine confirms the pause (POC §8).
An install/update run while take_open lands in install-refused-midtake and touches nothing (N9).

laws.title: The click is the door
laws.rule: **The click is the door** (N21) — no menus; the mushroom opens the one surface the moment needs. **A launch you did yourself is a click** (N41); launches shroom does itself stay silent: the login item opens nothing, and an update relaunch restores the window that was open before it and opens the popover by itself, under the mushroom, to say how the update went (B155). When the mushroom can't be seen, the popover drops from the top-right of the screen with the pointer; while the menu bar is hidden (a full-screen app, or set to hide) it opens where the mushroom rests (B161). A popover opens unasked only for a pause or stop you didn't make (N39) or after an update relaunch (B155) — and **an unasked popover never takes the keyboard**: a Return typed into another app stays there.
invariants: Left-click on the tray never shows a native menu in any state; in idle-unprovisioned it opens welcome (or member-welcome while an invite remembered under Later still lives, N30), in idle-ready it opens config, in recording it pauses (popover only after the pause is confirmed).
A user-initiated launch (Spotlight, Finder, Dock, a fresh install onto a Mac that remembers its space, the reopen event) yields exactly the transition a tray click yields in the same state.

A login-item launch opens no surface. An update relaunch restores only the window that was open before it, and opens the popover unasked with the update's one-shot status line (B155). Sole other exception: an install command carrying --join opens the invite (N41).

The popover an update relaunch opens is non-activating like every unasked popover, but a click anywhere else closes it, as it closes a popover you opened; the other unasked popovers stay until touched (B155, DEVIATIONS #39).
Popovers opened unasked (the auto-pause/auto-stop family) are non-activating: shroom's key-window/focus state is unchanged and a Return typed into the frontmost other app is not delivered to shroom.
When the status item is occluded, the popover is anchored at the top-right of the screen that has the pointer; a status item parked over a hidden menu bar anchors it where the item rests (B161).
Right-click yields the one-item native menu “Quit shroom” only in idle states; mid-take a right-click behaves as a click (surfaces table, N39).

laws.title: Dock iff a window is open
laws.rule: **Dock iff a window is open** (Region 1). Popovers never bring the dock icon.
invariants: For every state: dock_icon_visible == (number of open shroom windows > 0).
Opening or closing any popover, banner, or overlay (the countdown scrim, the bubble) never changes dock_icon_visible.
Popover-only states (config, paused, discard-confirm, quit-confirm, stopped-offline, stopped-stranded, auto-pause faces) with no window open have no dock icon.

Confirmed by Bagrat at the 0.1.10 checkpoint (B138): the Library, Settings and the setup window each bring the Dock icon while open, after setup too; with every window closed it goes, so a set-up shroom that opens or comes back from an update with no window shows none.

laws.title: Asks are banners, facts are the status line
laws.rule: **Asks are banners, facts are the status line** (N38) — one of each at most; the amber dot means *something needs you*, the Frost dot *something new from us*.
invariants: At any moment the popover shows at most one banner and at most one status line.
With several banner causes active, the shown banner is the highest of: a saved take > the space can't take videos > recording-off > an update (N38).
Banners carry the ask (an action); the status line carries facts only (upload truth, then one-shot lines) and no action button.

Tray face is exactly one of {plain, red dot, pause bars, amber, Frost}: red dot iff recording, pause bars iff paused, amber = something needs you (a saved take, the space can't take videos, recording off), Frost = an update is ready and is the lowest face — shown only when no other non-plain face applies (N37, N38).

laws.title: One default per surface, and Return triggers it
laws.rule: **One default per surface, and Return triggers it** (N38) — Start in `config`, Resume in `paused`; *click the mushroom, press Return* is the whole path to a recording. A banner's own filled button is never the Return default, and a focused field's Return belongs to its field (Invite in Members, Claim in `name`). Button order follows macOS — the default rightmost — except the ratified welcome pair, whose filled action comes first; its twins (`member-welcome`, `join-switch-confirm`) follow it, and so do the single-action faces (`stopped-stranded`, the saved-take banners), whose one filled button leads. *(A deliberate local exception — check it at ratification.)*
invariants: Each state has at most one default action, and Return activates exactly it: config → Start, paused → Resume.
From idle-ready with Start enabled, the event sequence tray-click, Return reaches countdown with no other input.

A banner's filled button (e.g. the saved-take banner's Get link, the update banner's Update) is never the Return target; Return in config with a banner showing triggers Start when Start is enabled, and nothing when a banner greys Start (member-revoked, space-gone).
With a text field focused, Return triggers that field's action: Members composer → Invite; name → Claim this name (and only once the charset check passes).

In every face that has a default/filled action among several buttons, the default is rightmost, except welcome, member-welcome, join-switch-confirm, stopped-stranded and the saved-take banners, whose filled action comes first.

laws.title: Destruction is never one stray keystroke away
laws.rule: **Destruction is never one stray keystroke away** (N23, N24) — destructive entry points are red text, never buttons; destructive questions are red-outlined, rightmost, never filled, with **no Return default**; Esc always means *back*.
invariants: Every destructive entry point (Discard…, Remove…, Delete…) renders as red text, never as a button.

Every destructive question (discard-confirm, the saved-take Discard… confirm, member-remove-confirm, the Library delete sheet, the Disconnect/Leave sheets) renders its destructive button red-outlined, rightmost, never filled.
In every destructive-question state, Return causes no transition (no Return default).
In every confirm/popover state, Esc maps to back (e.g. discard-confirm Esc → paused; click-away ≡ Back) and never to the destructive action.

laws.title: Nothing auto-copies
laws.rule: **Nothing auto-copies** (N1) — copying is always a visible button that reads “Copied”.
invariants: No transition writes the system clipboard unless it is a user-invoked copy (a visible Copy link button click; ⌘C in the Library, N35).
Entering the owner page after Stop/Get link, invite-born, stopped-offline, or any other state leaves the clipboard unchanged.
Every Copy link button reads “Copied” immediately after its click, then reverts.

laws.title: No dialog to an empty chair
laws.rule: **No dialog to an empty chair** (N17) — a macOS prompt appears only right after a click that asked for it; the monthly re-confirm is pulled forward to `config` so it never lands inside a take (N38).
invariants: Every macOS permission prompt (microphone, screen, camera) is requested only inside the handler of a user click that asked for it (e.g. Allow recording, a camera picked in the popover, Camera as the source).
done never fires a permission dialog on entry (N17).
No macOS prompt — including the monthly screen-recording re-confirm — appears while a take is open; the re-confirm is surfaced at config (the recording-off banner) before Start.

laws.title: Failures are states
laws.rule: **Failures are states** (N18) with scaffold-grade names and their own renders; guards that act as you type filter and never scold (N15).
invariants: Every blocking failure in the spec maps to a distinct kebab-case state id with its own render and its own set of enabled transitions (e.g. install-net-drop, install-checksum-fail, install-unsupported-os, install-refused-midtake, token-garbled, token-wrong-powers, gate-email, gate-card, name-taken, wizard-offline, the join failures).

As-you-type guards (the name charset filter) cause no state transition: rejected characters never land, uppercase lowercases silently, and no scolding/error line renders (only the quiet fading explanation).
wizard-offline auto-resumes on reconnect with no retry button.

laws.title: Secrets ride files
laws.rule: **Secrets ride files** under `~/.shroom`, mode 600 — never argv, chat, or logs. One scoped exception: a join link — a member's or an own-Mac one — once, in an install command (N3, N29, N33).
invariants: Every file under ~/.shroom that holds a secret has mode 0600.
No spawned argv, log line, or chat-facing text contains a token, temp credential, or device key — sole exception: a join link (member or own-Mac) passed once via --join in the install command.
Join links accepted on argv are one-time-use; member links expire after seven days, own-Mac links after one hour (N3, N33).
Stored secrets (the admin token, member/device credentials, an invite remembered under Later — N30) exist only as files under ~/.shroom, never in argv, chat, or logs.

laws.title: One space per Mac
laws.rule: **One space per Mac** (N31); **every Mac of the owner is owner-class** (N33); members own their videos, the owner sees all (N5).
invariants: A Mac is joined to at most one space at any time; moving to another space happens only through join-switch-confirm (blocked while uploads drain or a recovered take waits).
Every Mac joined via Add another Mac, and every Mac holding the token, has owner-class role: its Library can show all members' videos and it sees the Members tab.
A member Mac lists and manages only videos whose maker is that member; owner-class Macs see and can delete all.

laws.title: Product voice
laws.rule: **Product voice** — *your space · an invite · members · your link*; internals never surface (no error codes, no bucket, no Worker, no creds).
invariants: No user-visible string (window, popover, banner, sheet, page, Terminal output, tooltip) contains an error code (e.g. 10031) or the internals “bucket”, “Worker”, or “creds”/credentials (“Cloudflare” and “token” are product-facing in the wizard's ratified copy and are not banned; the workers.dev hostname inside a link is the link, not the internal noun — match “Worker” case-sensitively as a word).
User-facing copy names things with the product vocabulary: your space · an invite · members · your link.
Scope: the no-internals check covers said-lines, including the installer's header comment block (ratifiable copy, N11); the installer's inline source comments are exempt (technical but honest, N11).

laws.title: Numbers
laws.rule: **Numbers** — in the app's sentences, one to nine are words (“seven days”, “two videos are still uploading”, N28); compact facts keep figures (row facts like “5 days left”, counts like “14 videos”, lengths like “4:32”). The price facts are the deliberate two-register pair: numerals in the welcome, words on the landing's tiles (N12).
invariants: In the app's sentences, a standalone count from one to nine is spelled as a word (“seven days”, “two videos are still uploading”).
Compact facts keep figures: row facts (“5 days left”), counts (“14 videos”), lengths (“4:32”).
Price facts: numerals in the welcome, words on the landing's tiles (N12) — the deliberate two-register pair.

ledger.title: Landing page in v1's definition of done?
ledger.decision: **Yes — full page, curl-only.** One install path at launch: the readable script at `shroom.am/install`. brew formula + .dmg are post-v1 additions, absent from the v1 machine.
amended_by: N49 (install via Homebrew joins the install line in v1)

ledger.title: Record before cloud setup?
ledger.decision: **No — setup-first gate.** `Later` parks the app in `idle-unprovisioned`; Record routes to the wizard. No local-recording or local-library states exist in v1.

ledger.title: Start at login?
ledger.decision: **Pre-checked visible checkbox in the welcome panel.** Applied on panel dismissal (either button), changeable in settings, never registered silently.

ledger.title: First hostname label (the Worker's name, visible in every link)
ledger.decision: **`v`** — every link reads `v.<name>.workers.dev/<id>`; a custom domain (upgrade tier) hides the label entirely. Permanent once links exist. *Amended by N42 for one case: a clashing “v” becomes the label `shroom`.*
amended_by: N42 (amended for one case: a clashing “v” becomes the label shroom)

ledger.title: Permission timing
ledger.decision: **End of onboarding, same window** — mic inline → Settings switch → guided relaunch → priming warm-up. First Record is pure. Arm-time re-probe survives as a guard, not a step. (Reversed the walkthrough's first-arm rec — that rec was premised on the value-first U1 shape, which U1's decision rejected.)

ledger.title: The title moment at stop
ledger.decision: **On-page focused title, owner-cookie auth.** Stop opens `…/<id>?k=<one-time-key>` → the Worker validates, sets a long-lived owner cookie (space-scoped, likely HttpOnly), 302s to the clean URL — the address bar never holds the key. Owner-mode persists per-browser: opening your own link from Slack months later still edits. Shared links are always clean. *Amended by N40: the cookie names a member, and owner-mode is by role.*
amended_by: N40 (amended: the cookie names a member; owner-mode by role)

ledger.title: Clipboard at stop *(new question, leg 4)*
ledger.decision: **Never auto-copied.** Copying is explicit — [ Copy link ] on the page, Copy last link in the tray. *Tray door removed by N21 — the page and the Library row are the two doors.*
amended_by: N46 (Copy thumbnail, a third explicit copy)

ledger.title: Where "fully live" lands
ledger.decision: **The page itself is the signal.** The self-refreshing page carries live upload progress while the queue drains; the tray mirrors it. **No macOS notifications in v1** — zero notification-permission surface. *Since N21 the tray's mirror is the config popover's status line.*
amended_by: N21 (the tray mirror is now the config popover status line)

ledger.title: Sender identity on the page
ledger.decision: **Anonymous.** Schema carries a sender-name field from day one; no name UI in v1. The mark: a small shroom icon bottom-right, tooltip “made with shroom”, linking home — and in owner-mode it's toggleable **right on the page**, the setting applying space-globally.

ledger.title: Update posture
ledger.decision: **Notify-then-apply.** A tray badge announces the update; the user applies with one click. (Bagrat, against the auto-apply recommendation — consent over convenience.) *The apply row lives in the config popover since N21.*
amended_by: N21 (the apply row lives in the config popover)

ledger.title: Custom-domain timing *(new question, leg 5)*
ledger.decision: **Post-v1.0.** v1 is workers.dev-only; the Worker design keeps the attach door open; docs state the upgrade honestly.

ledger.title: Second-Mac join flow
ledger.decision: **Dissolved into the member model (N3):** the second Mac is a member you invite from the first — 30 s, no dashboard. Admin re-paste survives as the recovery door (“Found your space — 14 videos. This Mac is joined.”). *Amended by N33: the second Mac joins through Add another Mac, owner-class — not as a plain member.*
amended_by: N33 (amended: the second Mac joins through Add another Mac, owner-class)

ledger.title: Member model *(Bagrat reframe, leg 5)*
ledger.decision: **Ratified for v1.** The space is born multi-member: the pasted token is infra/admin setup and retires after it; recording always runs on member creds; the owner is silently member #1. Members join with zero Cloudflare anything — the C persona lands in v1. Join code may embed in the install command (zero-paste join; conscious argv/history exception — one-time-use, 7-day TTL).
amended_by: N33 (argv exception extended to own-Mac links)

ledger.title: Member write path
ledger.decision: **Worker-minted temp creds.** One cred shape for all: prefix-scoped ≤7-day S3 temp creds (probed); owner self-mints locally from the admin token, members mint via one authenticated Worker endpoint. **Minting is automatic and invisible for every role** (Bagrat's ratification condition). Bytes always direct to R2 — never proxied.

ledger.title: In-space authority
ledger.decision: **Own videos + admin sees all.** Members see/manage only their own; the admin (whose bucket and bill) sees the whole library, deletes anything, manages members.

ledger.title: Is the guided persona claimed publicly?
ledger.decision: **Claim it, second billing.** Landing leads with the dev story; a “Record together” section states the member story honestly — true without asterisks now (the card cliff exists only for the admin). *Placement amended by N6: the section dissolved into hero point six — the claim stands, promoted.*

ledger.title: Landing message architecture *(fat-marker leg 1)*
ledger.decision: **The hero carries the whole message:** a punchline in shroom's own words (“Screen recordings without the monthly seat. / Pay as you go — sometimes completely free.” — re-ratified 2026-10-13: no competitor's name on the page) + six-point explanation with eyeball-number tiles. Install block above the demo (the command is small and hides below a full-width player; recipient-loop visitors already saw the demo half work). Trust strip = open source · your-storage-your-bill · built-to-outlive-us (telemetry line cut).
amends: U6 (placement amended)

ledger.title: Demo video shape *(fat-marker leg 1)*
ledger.decision: **Self-recorded, record-only, single take, no editing.** The controls can't appear in their own take (config/countdown precede capture; the tray click *is* pause; the page opens post-take) — so the demo narrates its own start, shows the being-recorded life + one real task, and ends “I click stop — the page you're watching is what opened.” Setup never appears in the demo; the VM full-loop variant rejected as a stunt.

ledger.title: Issue-reporting second door *(fat-marker leg 2)*
ledger.decision: **Two doors in failure copy: the new-issue deep link + `issues@shroom.am`.** The alias is one Cloudflare Email Routing rule on the domain — zero operated service, works for members without GitHub accounts. The tiny opt-in proxy behind PRINCIPLES' opt-in telemetry stays parked with the post-v1 telemetry track. Scaffold nicety: the issue URL may prefill title/body via query params — everything visible in the URL.

ledger.title: Update-while-running semantics *(fat-marker leg 2)*
ledger.decision: **Quit → swap → relaunch; mid-take refuses.** Running but not mid-take: the script quits shroom, replaces the bundle, relaunches — tray-only, silent per the dock rule; the disk-backed upload queue rides through. Mid-take — recording **or paused** (a paused take is live) — polite refusal, nothing touched: the sacred-recording law reaches into the installer. Never swap under a running process (signature-mismatch kill on next load — verify exact behavior at scaffold). Classification via the app's machine-readable status seam, not process-sniffing. *Refined by N41: a fresh install onto a Mac that remembers its space opens the door; this update lane stays silent.*

ledger.title: Install progress posture *(fat-marker leg 2)*
ledger.decision: **curl's native bar for the app fetch.** The pasted one-liner keeps `-fsSL` — it fetches only the tiny script. The in-script app download shows curl's own progress bar: native terminal idiom, zero custom code in the readable source. Stillness rejected (indistinguishable from a hang on slow links); hand-rolled ticker rejected (cursor-control code in read-it-first source).

ledger.title: Installer source comments as copy *(fat-marker leg 2)*
ledger.decision: **A said-line surface.** “Read it first” makes the source a first-class audience page — the one page a skeptic reads slowly. The header comment block is ratifiable copy (plain-speech what-it-does); inline comments stay technical but honest. One screenful mocked and ratified with this screen.

ledger.title: Welcome dismissal semantics *(fat-marker leg 3)*
ledger.decision: **✕-close ≡ Later, exactly — no special case.** Any dismissal (either button or the close control) registers the login item iff the visible box is still checked; U4 refined. Copy correction: “**set up** your Cloudflare” (was “connect”). “Storage” here vs the landing's “account”, and numerals vs words, stand as deliberate two-register choices.
amends: U4 (refined)
amended_by: N30 (adds the “Have an invite link?” line under the welcome buttons)

ledger.title: Wizard plan panel + `account` screen *(fat-marker leg 4)*
ledger.decision: **Plan glyphs, not checkboxes:** → current · ✓ done · • still ahead — checkboxes read as something the user must click. Box 1 reworded: the Google sign-in alternative named in-panel (promoted from docs-only), “Adding it costs nothing”, and the free ceiling made concrete (“up to about six hours of video” — the welcome register). Box 3 gains the example `v.yourname.workers.dev`. **I have one** = filled rightmost default; after “Not yet” opens signup the screen deliberately doesn't morph — self-report by proceeding stands. *Box-1 wording amended by N14 — the card content moved to its own row. The no-morph is reversed by N19 (`account-signing-up`).*
amended_by: N48 (the free ceiling is about three hours)

ledger.title: The card step + token-screen posture *(fat-marker leg 5)*
ledger.decision: **The plan grows a fifth row and the gates move into it.** Box 1 ticks at proceed — the plan's one self-reported tick (nothing is probeable pre-token; the paste proves it moments later). New row: “A credit card for storage (their rule, not a charge — free up to about six hours of video)”; box 1 slims to the sign-in gate — the visible card row *is* the pre-warn now. Card step: email check first (`gate-email`), then card presence (`gate-card`, button **Add credit card**); auto-poll spinner (polling dots rejected — read as a carousel); both clear → row ticks. Token screen never auto-opens the browser: read → **[ Create token in Cloudflare ]** (the only trigger, serves every retry) → paste; the wrong-powers line points back at it.
amends: N13 (box-1 wording)

ledger.title: The setup window after the first stranger run: the email first, the card watched, the token box still, and the permissions before the wiring
ledger.decision: **Bagrat, on the canvas (2026-10-15: all four boards approved, to be built), after CHECKPOINT §10's first two-VM run.** (1) Cloudflare makes no token until the account's email is confirmed, and shroom can't see that before it has one: the signup trip says to confirm the email first, and the token step reached through “I signed up” carries one quiet reminder under the field until a paste lands. (2) The card gate keeps its line and Add credit card; one quiet line under the button says where it goes and that shroom is watching — another once the button was clicked. ledger.title: Voice cuts: say “shroom cut”, say the line again, and the slip is cut
ledger.decision: **Bagrat asked for it, 2026-10-18** (relayed by the orchestrator), and tried it with his own voice the same day: the cut worked. (1) **The cue.** A speaker who slips says “shroom cut” on its own and says the line again. When the space listens (N66: the space's own Cloudflare account hears each take as it uploads), the Mac that made the take reads the take's transcript once it is whole and finds each cue. “shroom” is matched by sound, so the way it was heard doesn't matter, and it must be followed by “cut”. A mention (“just say shroom cut”, “the shroom cut feature”) is left alone; a looser hearing (“Troom cut”) counts only when it stands as a sentence of its own. A cue heard where the take on the Mac is quiet, its words and half a second either side all but silent, was never said: the hearing wrote it into silence (it does, on a take with no speech in it, primed with the cue), and it is left alone (2026-10-25, after a take of Bagrat's on the early build cut its silent start). (2) **The cut.** The words after the cue are lined up against the words before it to find where the line was started again; the cut runs from that restart through the cue, its edges set in the quiet on either side, found in the take on the Mac. A retake that says enough of the slip again is cut at once. A cue that breaks off a sentence (it stops without a full stop, or on a word no sentence ends on: “the”, “and”, “to”, “will”, or “is” after a noun, as in “…and your link is”) takes the sentence with it, back to its start, when it began within 20 s; the finished sentence before it stays, even when the speaker ran straight on from it. Unless the judgment below hears all of that sentence said again after the cue (a start scored 0.4 or more at the sentence's own start or before it), nothing was said again: the sentence is cut as the line before the cue, and the strip asks the owner to check it; a cue with nothing said again never has more than itself cut unasked (2026-10-25, after a take of Bagrat's on the early build said “shroom cut” with no slip, inside a sentence he carried on, and had the half before it cut unasked). A line said again in other words is weighed by meaning (Bagrat, 2026-10-18, relayed by the orchestrator: the mechanism deterministic, the judgment above it): the Mac lists the places the redone stretch might begin, within 20 s before the cue: the starts of up to three sentences, and the pauses of 0.4 s or more inside the cue's own sentence that leave at least three of its words before them (a finished sentence before it is redone whole or not at all); the space's own Cloudflare account (Clef) scores whether what was said after the cue says again everything from each; the cut runs from the farthest start scored 0.4 or more, and only ever reaches farther back than the words alone would. When it can't answer (the free day used up, a busy model), the words alone decide. When nothing was said again after a cue, how far back the slip went isn't clear: the line before the cue is cut with it, and the strip asks the owner to check (Bagrat, 2026-10-18, after a take of his own on the early build: cut the likely slip at once instead of offering it). (3) **Where it lands.** The cuts go into the record's edit list (N63) once per take, so the share page, the embed and the download follow them, as do the captions and chapters made from the same transcript (N66). The words cut stay out of what viewers get. Only a take stopped while the space listens is cut; nothing already shared changes. (4) **No switch of its own.** The space's listening (N66) is the one switch: the cue is a deliberate command, and a take without it is untouched. (5) **The owner page shows them** (`owner-page-cuts`), under the player, in owner-mode only: each cut's time and what was said, struck through, between a few words of what plays around it, with Put back; the line cut before a cue with nothing said again after it shows “shroom cut” struck as well, under a note asking the owner to check it, and its Put back brings the line back while “shroom cut” stays out (both his picks on the board, 2026-10-18). A press saves at once; one that doesn't save puts the row back and says so. They are reviewed in both places (Bagrat, 2026-10-18, relayed by the orchestrator: “Both”): the strip on the owner page for a quick check, and the editor's timeline (N63) for fine-tuning, the cuts as red parts, a cut put back dashed, to be cut again; both read and write the one edit list, so a Put back in either shows in the other. Viewers see only the cut video. (6) **The hint** (`owner-page-cue-hint`; Bagrat OK'd its line 2026-10-18, relayed by the orchestrator): in a space that listens, the owner page of a take with no voice cuts says how, under the player, until Got it or a first take with voice cuts. (7) **Finishing** (`uploading`, `hearing`; Bagrat, 2026-10-18 (relayed by the orchestrator): one indicator on the owner page, from the upload until the voice cuts land, “Finishing” his pick of its first word): the owner page's upload line becomes one line from go-live, “Finishing your video — the link already works, share it anytime.”, a small spinner turning in front of it and no bar (Bagrat, 2026-10-18 (relayed by the orchestrator): a small spinner in front of the words, no bar), resting beside a stalled upload's line; in a space that listens it stays after the upload, its spinner turning, while the take is heard, five minutes at most, and it fades when the cuts land (the strip takes its place), when there are none (the hint, while it's due), or when the five minutes pass. It never speaks of cuts. No “Ready ✓” after it (B142's, retired on the page) and no second line. The words are proposals until he OKs them. Built: DECISIONS B200, B201, B202, B203.

ledger.title: shroom on the command line, for a person or their coding agent
ledger.decision: **Proposed 2026-10-18 (dev/proposals/cli-agent-skill.md). Bagrat's calls the same day, relayed by the orchestrator:** an agent may start and stop recordings only once a Settings switch is on, off by default; a refused recording says so, says that switch turns it on, and gives a link that opens Settings right at it; the command may make invites; the command is always installed; it does things many at once, so an agent can invite a team or tidy many videos in one step; and it is built in full now, its release his to time. (1) **The `shroom` command** ships inside the app (`Contents/MacOS/shroom-cli`) and follows the app it ships in: that app's folder (a dev build's command reads `~/.shroom-dev`) and that app to open. The install line links it into `~/.local/bin` (and puts that folder on the login profile's PATH when it isn't there), the cask into Homebrew's bin; `--uninstall` takes both back. (2) **It works whether the app runs or not:** list, info, links, open, rename, delete, cleanup candidates, members, invites — through the space's own page under this Mac's device key, never the Cloudflare token. A delete, a member's removal or a batch invite changes nothing without `--yes`; a rename, delete, invite or removal waits while a take is open (law 4). (3) **Many at once:** a batch takes its items as arguments or from a file and answers each with its own status; it is safe to run again (nothing is done twice), and says so when only some went through. At most 20 invites or 100 items a call. Each person invited gets their own link: shroom sends nothing. (4) **Cleanup candidates** are the page's own suggestions where the page makes them, and otherwise the videos older than a number of days. (5) **Recording goes through the running app** (its control socket in shroom's folder, this user only): start is the popover's Start, countdown and permission beat included, the popover open or not; pause is the tray's; Resume and Stop are the paused popover's; a stop answers with its link (law 3: this stop made it; law 10: nothing is copied). The app answers with a code, and the command says the words. (6) **Settings → General gains “Your coding agent”**: the prompt to paste, Copy (“Copied”, law 10), Read it first (shroom.am/cli), the line under them, and the switch “Let it start and stop recordings”, off by default; while it's off the app refuses every recording ask. **The refusal is three lines:** recording from a coding agent is off; the switch in Settings, under General, turns it on; and the link `shroom://settings/agent` (with `--json`, also its own field, `settings_link`; exit 10 as before). Bagrat approved its words and the switch's label as drawn, 2026-10-18. Clicked, the link opens shroom if it isn't running, and Settings on General with the switch's row in view and lit for a moment; the switch stays as it was — only the person flips it. Mid-take it opens nothing (law 4); a sheet open in Settings stays, and Settings comes forward as it stands. Settings needs a space (B160), so a Mac without one is told to set shroom up first, before the switch comes up. (7) **shroom.am/cli** is the guide an agent reads (a skill's SKILL.md), and `shroom guide` prints the same; /agent points there. (8) **Without the count, and the label** (Bagrat, 2026-10-18): `record start --no-countdown` starts the take at once, capture beginning as the count's end would; the app's own Start keeps its count. A take the command starts shows a small label at the top right of the display it records — “Your coding agent is recording your screen” — while it records (paused, it goes; a take of the camera only has none), left out of the video and taking no clicks; `--no-label` leaves it off. The tray shows every take, whatever the flags. Bagrat approved the label's board as drawn — its look, its words and the label on by default — 2026-10-18. Built: DECISIONS B215–B219. Ratified by Bagrat, 2026-10-18: the Settings card's words as built (he'll tweak them once he uses it), the command's words and the guide as built.

ledger.title: The page counts plays in the owner's own account, and the Library suggests videos to clean up
ledger.decision: **Bagrat asked for it, 2026-10-18**: shroom is pay-as-you-go, so it should say which videos are worth deleting, from how old they are, how often and how far they've been watched and when last. **The same day he chose**: plays counted **on by default**, with the switch in Settings; **plays and unique-ish viewers** both counted; the score is **fading and cost together**; deleting from the suggestions is **one tap with Undo**; and the rest to the build's judgment (B210–B214). (1) **The page counts plays.** A viewer's page and the embed send one beacon at the first play and one each time the tab hides, saying how much was watched; the Worker keeps per-video counts in the space's own bucket — plays, unique-ish viewers (a day-only hash under a salt replaced daily), how far each was watched in tenths, plays per day, last played. No cookie, nothing stored on the viewer's device, nothing kept that says who watched. The maker's own page never counts. A video that isn't live gets no record; a deleted one's record goes with its seal. (2) **Settings → General gains a group, Your videos**: **Count plays** (on; the space's switch, owner-class only, as the mark's is), **Suggest videos to clean up** (on; this Mac's), and **Space used** (the space's size, and what it costs past Cloudflare's free 10 GB). (3) **A video is suggested** when counting has watched it at least 30 days, it is at least 30 days old and nobody has played it in 30, its plays have faded (each counts half as much every 30 days, weighted by how far it was watched: 0.3 + 0.7 × its median share) below a quarter of one fresh full watch, and it takes at least a cent a month to keep at list price (about 0.67 GB). Never one marked Keep. The costliest per remaining play comes first. (4) **The Library says so in one line** above the rows, with Review… and ✕ (not now, until the list changes). (5) **Suggested to clean up** is the Library's own view: what deleting all of them frees and saves, then each video with when it was made, its size and why ("Watched 4 times, the last 10 months ago"), with Open page, Keep and Delete. **Delete is one tap**: the row goes and an Undo line stays a few seconds before the delete is sent; Delete all… asks once with the several-videos sheet. Keep takes a video off the list for good (the record's `keep`). (6) **The money line** gives sizes always, and cents only past the free 10 GB; inside it, the saving reads as nothing yet, and a clean-up that brings the space back inside it says so. (7) **shroom.am/privacy's line on viewers changes**; its new words, from the board "shroom.am/privacy — the viewers' line once plays are counted", Bagrat approved on 2026-10-18 with the sentence on the one-day viewer stand-in, and the page carries them (site/pages/privacy.html). (8) **Each suggested row says what it costs a month**, only when the space is past the free 10 GB and never on a member's Mac (Bagrat, 2026-10-18): its size at the list price (B212). Built: DECISIONS B210–B214. **Bagrat ratified it as built, 2026-10-18**: its words and rules, and B211's 1¢ size gate.

ledger.title: The space names its videos, adds chapters and writes captions, through the owner's own Cloudflare
ledger.decision: **B171's plan, built** (Bagrat, 2026-10-18, relayed by the orchestrator: build it now, decide the release later; the build's calls are made on judgment and listed in DECISIONS B205–B208 for him to overturn). (1) **Off until the owner turns it on, on the Mac that holds the setup key, and visible** (Bagrat, 2026-10-18: off by default, not to spend the AI allowance, but very visible; one switch for every AI feature): a banner in the popover, like the update's, says what shroom can do — name videos, add chapters, cut slips — and Turn on… opens a short confirm that says what it costs, once; the switch in Settings · Space, “AI for new videos”, is its home, and covers voice cuts (N65) too. Not now hides the banner for good on that Mac (Bagrat, 2026-10-18: from then on only the switch turns AI on). Turning it on re-wires the space's page with Cloudflare's AI and a schedule that runs each minute; the owner's key needs no new power (B171's live check 2). Turning it off takes them away; names, chapters and captions already made stay. Only new videos (Bagrat, 2026-10-18: no offer to name earlier ones). Members' Macs never show it and never see a cost. (2) **Each take is heard as it uploads**: every Mac tells the space when another minute of a take is up and once more after Stop, and the space hears that minute and keeps its words beside the take, on the recording's own clock. (3) **The title comes early, the rest after Stop** (Bagrat, 2026-10-18: the title must be there when the page opens): once the first minute is heard while the take records, a title from it alone, so the page opens named; after Stop the space names the take again from all of it and places its chapters, from the words that play: the title while nobody has typed one (a typed title always wins and is never written over), chapters only on a video of 90 s or more with two or more, and captions from the same words, never a second hearing. (4) **The free day**: every Cloudflare account gets 10,000 neurons a day (about 2½ hours of new video; Bagrat, 2026-10-18); when they run out, the rest waits and is finished after 00:00 UTC by the space's schedule, with no error anywhere; on a paid account it simply runs (about 4¢ per video hour). (5) **Edits never re-hear** (the editor, N63, when it lands): chapters and captions follow the saved edit on every view; the name and chapters are made again only when an edit removes at least a fifth of what was said or a whole chapter. **The turn-on, ratified** (Bagrat, 2026-10-18): he approved the banner, its confirm, its turning-on, failed and on faces and the switch in Settings · Space as drawn (AiBanner, AiConfirm, AiBannerStates, AiSettings), with the price said “per video hour” so it reads as hours of video, not of the day; he may tweak the words later. **The landing's line, agreed** (Bagrat, 2026-10-18), goes on shroom.am with the homepage's redesign, not before: “AI titles, chapters and captions are free for about 2½ hours of new video a day. Recording more? About 4¢ per video hour on Cloudflare’s $5 plan.” **The privacy page's AI point, approved** (Bagrat, 2026-10-18), as drafted on the board AiPrivacy. The rest is provisional: its words are drafts until he OKs them.

ledger.title: The editor: trim, cut, undo, and edits the link plays
ledger.decision: **Bagrat asked for it, 2026-10-18** (relayed by the orchestrator): a real editor, apart from AI, that the spoken-cue layer can plug into later. **Edit… in a Library row's menu** opens the **editor**, a window of its own (one at a time), on a live video in this Mac's scope, renamable here: the video plays at the top; under it the play button and the time, edited position / edited length, with “was 4:32” once the edit changes the length; then the **timeline**: the whole recording's sound as a waveform with the playhead, **yellow ends that drag to trim**, and **a drag across the sound that selects a part**, with **Cut 12.0 s** under it. **A cut shows red** and the preview skips it as it plays; clicking a cut offers **Put back**. **Undo and Redo** (also ⌘Z and ⇧⌘Z) step through every change made in the window, Put back and Revert included. **Revert to original** puts back every cut and both ends. **Done** (Return) saves the edit and closes the window; ✕ is Done. The footer says the link stays the same. Saving is a small edit list kept in the video's record; **the share page and the embed apply it as they play** (they skip the cuts, hold to the trim, and show the edited length), so **the link never changes** and nothing is re-encoded first. Until then the original stays in the space, so Revert works from any Mac. Then the window stays to make **the final video**: the Mac cuts the edit with its own encoder and puts it up beside the original under the same link (“Making the final video… 40%”; the window can be closed and shroom finishes it); once it is up, Download and the page use it. **Then it asks “Delete the original?”** (Bagrat, 2026-10-18: encourage deleting it soon; no 30-day keep): **Yes, delete** leads, filled — a click, never Return (law 9; DEVIATIONS #55, ratified 2026-10-18) — and the edit becomes the video for good; **Keep for 2 days** keeps the original so the edit can still be reverted, and shroom deletes it after two days, whether or not this Mac is open then; closing the window there means Keep for 2 days. While the original is kept, the editor says by Revert how long it has left; once it is gone, the edit is final and Revert to original only undoes what changed since the window opened. A video that isn't on this Mac comes from the space first (“Getting the video from your space…”); if that fails the window says so and offers Try again. While it saves, Done reads Saving…; if the save doesn't go through, the window stays open and says so, and Done tries again. Edit… greys offline and while a take is open (law 4), as Rename does. Built: DECISIONS B195, B197. **Ratified by Bagrat as built, 2026-10-18**, with B195–B199 and the build’s words.

ledger.title: shroom edit: the command trims and cuts a video, and the app makes its final video
ledger.decision: **The orchestrator, 2026-10-19:** the shroom command gains `edit` now that the editor (N63) has shipped, built in full with its words provisional for Bagrat's next look. (1) **`shroom edit <video>` says what the edit is**: how long the video plays and how long the recording is, the trim, each cut by its id (`m1`… by hand, `v1`… from the voice cues) with where it starts and ends and whether it's applied (a voice cue's cut can be a suggestion, not applied), and whether the final video is made. (2) **One change a call**, on the recording's own clock (seconds, or minutes:seconds): `trim <in> <out>`, `cut <start> <end>`, `put-back <cut>`, `apply <cut>`, `resize <cut> <start> <end>`, `revert`. Each is the editor's own step (B195), refused for the editor's own reasons, and saved at once as the editor's Done saves: the list in the video's record, so the link plays it from its next load and nothing is re-encoded first. `--dry-run` says what the edit would be and saves nothing. Undo and Redo stay the editor's: a window's history, never a record's. (3) **It goes where `rename` goes**: through the space's page under this Mac's device key, the owner's Macs on any video and a member's Mac on its own (B215); it waits while a take is open (law 4); and while that video is open in an editor window on this Mac it changes nothing (`editor_open`), so that window's Done never silently undoes it. The last save wins, as between two editors (B195). (4) **The final video is the app's to make**: after a change that leaves something out, the command asks the running app, opening it as the record commands do (`--no-launch` leaves it), and the app makes it as it makes one after the editor's Done, one at a time and never over a take, getting the video from the space first when this Mac hasn't got it; Download and the page use it once it's up, and the original is kept two days, then goes (B197: Keep for 2 days, the command never deleting an original itself). `shroom edit <video> finish` asks again, for a change saved while the app wasn't there. A change back to the whole recording needs no final video. (5) **Its answers**: the edit as (1) says it; a refusal is `cant_edit` with its reason (`out_of_range`, `leaves_too_little`, `too_short`, `nothing_changes`, `no_such_cut`, `editor_open`), exit 12; the words are the command's own (`say.rs`). ledger.title: Setup shows its waits as they happen, and wiring finishes on its own
ledger.decision: **A tester's finding, 2026-10-19** (a fresh Cloudflare account, 0.1.26): two waits in the setup felt stuck — the card step and the last step — and nearly lost him. **Bagrat, 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25** (relayed by the orchestrator), on the boards “Setup — the card step shows its check as it runs…” and “Setup — the last step shows each part of wiring as it lands…”: (1) **The card step's check** shows its four parts under the card row as they run — Your token works · Your Cloudflare email is confirmed · Storage is switched on · Looking for your link name and any earlier space… — each ticking only when its own probe answers, never ahead of it. (2) **After Add credit card**, the watch is a row of its own: “Waiting for Cloudflare to confirm your card is in place…” with its running clock; from 45 s one quiet line: “A new card can take Cloudflare a minute or so to count. Once it's added, I'll move on — hang tight!” (3) **The last step** lists wiring's five parts under the calm line — Your private storage · Your video page · Your name is on · Last check passed · Adding this Mac to your space… — the part underway with its running clock, counted from the first try and never reset by a retry; from 3 min on the name, one quiet line: “New names can take Cloudflare a while longer, sometimes ten minutes. It's fine to close this window — I'll finish by myself.” While the permissions are the step, the wiring row's aside names the part underway, with its clock. (4) **Clocks on spinning rows only**: never on a done row or one still to come; a part that answers inside a second ticks before its clock shows. (5) **Wiring finishes on its own** (Bagrat, 2026-10-19: “finish on its own”): while a token is saved, the name row has ticked and no space is set up, wiring keeps trying with the window open or closed, and from the next launch after a quit (the login item's silent one included, its probe pass saying where the setup stands); it opens nothing when it lands (laws 5, 11), and the next click on the mushroom opens the popover ready to record — or the setup at the permissions, when they aren't done on this Mac. No step is stored (law 1): what's done is what the calls answered this time. **Ratified by Bagrat as drawn, 2026-10-25**; the forms the boards didn't draw (a part still to come, a part underway that the board drew done) are the build's, provisional. The last part of each run has no done form: the step moves on the moment it answers (the check to the next row, wiring to all set), so “Looked for your link name and any earlier space” and “This Mac is in your space”, on the boards' notes, never show and aren't lines. ledger.title: Pin to keep, Delete all, and auto-cleanup run by the space's page
ledger.decision: **Bagrat, 2026-10-19**, after a private-round tester said most videos stop mattering within weeks: add Delete all to the suggested list and pinned videos. **2026-10-24**: yes to real auto-cleanup on the tester's terms, the space's own page doing the deleting so a closed Mac never misses one (relayed by the orchestrator), and a heads-up in the popover too; the same day he approved every board as drawn (the boards “Library — pin a video to keep it”, “Library — Suggested to clean up: Pin in place of Keep, Delete all…”, “The shroom command — shroom pin / shroom unpin”, “Settings — General: auto-cleanup…”, “Library — auto-cleanup's warning…”, “Library and the command — after auto-cleanup deletes…”, “Popover — auto-cleanup under the tray icon…”). (1) **Pin** is the record's `keep` (N68's Keep, renamed so one idea has one name): a pinned video is never suggested and never deleted by auto-cleanup. A row's menu says Pin or Unpin after Rename, at once, no sheet; several rows selected, it acts on all. A pinned row shows a small pin before its title. Suggested to clean up's Keep becomes Pin. `shroom pin` / `shroom unpin` do the same, many at once; list and info say “pinned”. (2) **Delete all…** on the suggested list asks once with its own sheet — the count and what it frees — then every row leaves at once and one Undo line holds the whole batch for the few seconds a single delete's does. Pinned videos are never in the list; one pinned elsewhere since the list was read is skipped. (3) **Auto-cleanup**, off by default: Settings · General's Your videos gains “Delete videos nobody watches” — Off · After 15 days · After 30 days · After 60 days — counted from the last time someone watched it (the owner's own plays never count), or from its upload if nobody did, never before counting began. It's the space's setting, for every video in it, and is set on the Mac that holds the setup key, because turning it on gives the space's page its schedule (the one Cron Trigger AI naming uses, B206); every other Mac reads it. It needs Count plays: with counting off it greys and nothing goes. Turning it on, or shortening it, while videos already qualify asks once, with how many and the date; nothing goes sooner than three days after. (4) **Three days ahead** the Library says which videos will be deleted and when, each going row with a one-tap Pin; Review… shows them first. The popover shows the same as a banner, with Pin both (all of them) and Review…, Not now hiding it on that Mac until the list changes. (5) **The space's page deletes** what's due, on the date or within a day of it, whether any Mac is open or not, one video a run: never a pinned one, one still uploading, one open in an editor (the Mac marks it), or one watched since its warning. It goes as a Delete does: the link says the video was removed. (6) **After**, the Library and the popover say once what went and what it freed, with OK. Built: DECISIONS B232–B234.

ledger.title: AI is on by default, and said once
ledger.decision: **Bagrat, 2026-10-25** (relayed by the orchestrator, on the boards “Popover — AI features are turned on…” and its states), reversing N66's off by default (2026-10-18): the space's AI — names, chapters, captions and voice cuts, one switch — is **on by default**. (1) **A space set up from now on starts with it on**: the setup's wiring puts up a new page with Cloudflare's AI and its schedule, and says nothing about it (Bagrat, 2026-10-25: nothing in the setup, nor in the Library); the switch in Settings · Space shows it on. A repair's wiring never changes it. (2) **A space set up before**: on the Mac that holds the setup key, the first popover after the update that would show the AI's banner turns it on as it shows “AI features are turned on.” with Turn off and OK — so nothing is heard before it's been said (`ai-turned-on`). It stays until OK or Turn off; Turn off re-wires the page without the AI and says so once (`ai-turning-off`, `ai-turn-off-failed`, `ai-off`). ledger.title: Turning AI on or off shows its parts as they happen
ledger.decision: **Bagrat's hand test of 0.1.30-early.1, 2026-10-25**: turning AI on or off took long enough to worry, with little shown while it ran — the anxiety a tester named in the setup (N74). **Bagrat, 2026-10-25** (relayed by the orchestrator, on the boards “Settings — Space: the AI switch while it works…” and “Popover — AI features are turned on: Turn off while it works…”, with the plainer words): (1) **The switch moves at once** to where it's going, greyed while the page is re-wired. (2) **Three parts list under its cost line**, each ticking only when its own calls answer, the one underway spinning with its running clock from its first second, as N74's do: “Checking your space…” → “Your space is ready”; “Connecting AI to your space…” → “AI connected” (off: “Disconnecting AI…” → “AI disconnected”); “Switching AI on for new videos…” → “AI is on for new videos” (off: “Switching AI off for new videos…” → “AI is off for new videos”). (3) **Done is when the page itself says so** (its ping answers with the AI on, or without it); the last part ticks in bold and the list stays until the window closes or the tab changes. (4) **Didn't go through** (law 12): the switch reads as the page has it and is live again; the part that stopped carries a cross in its plain words, with “Couldn't change that just now — try again in a moment.” under the list. (5) **Running long**: from 20 s on one part, one quiet line, “Cloudflare is slower than usual just now — hang tight.”; the clock keeps going until the re-wiring's 3 min deadline, which is a didn't-go-through. Five minutes after the go-live at most, by the page's own count, as before; a name that comes later still drops in. A strip whose cuts land first shows under the player with the line still under it. It never says a name is coming, and no new words are added. Words waiting for the next free day don't keep it (the note under the title says the rest comes later). (2) **The title shimmers while the name is on its way**: a soft gradient slides in the empty title field beside its placeholder, for as long as the line lasts. ledger.title: A click on a control that something late just moved does nothing

In the popover and in Settings, for **half a second** after something lands and moves a control or puts a new one in its place — a banner, an Update button, a line under a picker — a pointer click on that control does nothing, and the next click works. What the person's own click or key just changed (a menu they opened, a tab they picked, a pick that adds its line) is theirs and isn't held back; the keyboard is never held back (its focus doesn't move with the layout). Not a state and no words: the click is simply not taken. B and C (the offer below Start; the offer waiting for the next open) were not picked.

amendments.summary: The landing's separate "Record together" section dissolves into the hero's team point: "Your team just accepts an invite and records — no Cloudflare setup for them." The claim stands, promoted into the hero.

amendments.summary: Designed 2026-09-30, awaiting ratification. Silence applies only to launches shroom does itself (the login item, the update relaunch). A launch the user does (Spotlight, Finder, the Dock, a fresh install onto a Mac that still remembers its space) acts exactly as a tray click. The `updating` lane stays silent, except that an install command carrying --join opens the invite.

open_notes: Hero point count, to check at ratification: the spec calls the hero a 'six-point explanation' and the team line 'point six' (lines 54, 205, 1658). The ratified hero draws only five dashed points, and 'tiles between points three and four' matches five-point numbering. Either a point is missing or the count is wrong.

Law 8's welcome exception is flagged in the spec: 'A deliberate local exception — check it at ratification.' The welcome pair's filled action (Set up my space) comes first rather than rightmost. Its Return default is derived from Law 8 (N38, designed 2026-09-30, awaiting ratification); Region 1 itself never names a Return key (Law 8 is lines 136-143).

Copy status of the Terminal failure lines: the `installing` heading ratifies copy only for 'stream + source header'. The N18 table's column is headed 'Said-line draft', so install-net-drop, install-checksum-fail, install-unsupported-os, updating and install-refused-midtake lines are marked draft, including the mid-take refusal quoted in the N9 update-path block (lines 233, 254-263).
The mid-take refusal appears twice: as two lines in the update-path blockquote (254-255) and as one line in the N18 table (263). The fixture uses the two-line form.

The invite door on the welcome (N30) is designed, not ratified, and amends the ratified welcome. The spec says the join page's Open shroom deep link is the main road, and this paste door is its fallback (and the agent persona's) (lines 334-341).

N41 amends Region 1's 'every launch is silent' and is awaiting ratification. A launch the user does (Spotlight, Finder, the Dock, a fresh install onto a Mac that remembers its space) acts as a tray click. This is also the rescue when a crowded menu bar hides the mushroom behind the notch (lines 300-306).

Open question: N41 and Law 5 say an update relaunch restores whatever window was open before it. Region 1 says the script's `updating` lane relaunches tray-only and silent. Whether the restore applies to the script lane is not stated (lines 89, 128-129, 248-249, 304).

Retired copy that must NOT appear in idle-unprovisioned: the former Record-routed context line “Your first video is one setup away — about five minutes, once.” (retired with the menu by N21, lines 352-353).

Region 6 extends Region 1 states (lines 1462-1474). In the member lane, `installing` forwards --join to the app at launch. On a fresh Mac the app opens at `member-welcome` instead of `welcome`. If shroom is already installed, the `updating` lane runs and the relaunched app opens the invite (`member-welcome`, `join-already-here` or `join-switch-confirm`). Mid-take gives `install-refused-midtake` and the link stays unused. These are designed, not ratified.
Law 10 ('copying is always a visible button that reads “Copied”') is a standing law, but Region 1 doesn't draw a Copied face for the landing's [ Copy ] button. No 'Copied' said-line was invented.

The landing's page chrome is given only as '🍄 shroom wordmark left · GitHub link right.' The 🍄 is likely the mock stand-in for the logo (spec header, lines 18-20). The GitHub link's wording is not specified.
The demo id 'b4kq9d' is illustrative ('real space; id illustrative').

Personas: the dev walks Region 1 alone. The guided persona's agent overlays narration on the same machine; Region 6 defines the overlay, not a second machine (lines 169-170). Entry arrow 3 into the landing is the agent fetching the BYO-agent skill.

The welcome's two-register choices are ratified as-is: 'storage' on the welcome vs 'account' on the landing, and numerals ('30 hours') on the welcome vs words ('about thirty hours') on the landing tile. Tests must not normalize them (lines 331-333, Law 16).

There are no Fat-marker status notes in Region 1. Deliberately absent: brew and .dmg lanes (post-v1), any local recording before setup (U1), and the min-OS floor and Intel stance (scaffold-time facts) (lines 377-381).
All apostrophes in Region 1's said-lines are straight ASCII (') in the spec; quote marks around lines are curly “ ” and are stripped. Tests should match the spec's straight apostrophes.

scaffold_flags.flag: The system-requirements sentence's shape is ratified. The macOS floor and the Intel stance are scaffold-time facts (SCK matrix): fill the facts into the ratified shape without rewording, and state them plainly on the page once known. The same floor is the N in install-unsupported-os.
/install never redirects: architecture dispatch lives inside the script ("this address serves one file, and this is it"). The same URL serves the source view, so one URL serves two audiences.
The temporary download lands under ~ ("nothing outside your home folder"), and the app is placed in ~/Applications with no admin password.

The pasted one-liner keeps -fsSL and fetches only the tiny script. The app download inside the script uses curl's native progress bar (N10): no hand-rolled ticker or cursor-control code in the source people are told to read first.
The script always ends by opening the app (no quarantine ⇒ no prompt). No Gatekeeper, no admin password, nothing signing-shaped on the machine.
The OS version probe runs before the fetch (install-unsupported-os). A checksum mismatch is never installed. A re-run after a net drop is idempotent.
Mid-take classification reads the app's machine-readable status seam (the agent overlay's seam, the same door) and never sniffs the process. Recording and paused both refuse, and nothing is touched.

Update lane: quit → swap → relaunch, tray-only and silent. The disk-backed upload queue rides through. Never swap under a running process (a signature mismatch kills it on the next load; verify the exact behavior at scaffold).
The issue link in failure copy may prefill title and body through query params, with everything visible in the URL (N8 scaffold nicety).
The dock icon shows iff a shroom window is open. The tray mushroom appears from the first launch onward regardless. Popovers never bring the dock icon (Law 6).

Login item (U4/N12): the checkbox is visible and checked by default. The item is registered at panel dismissal (Set up my space, Later or ✕) iff the box is still checked. Never silent; changeable in settings.
Set up my space morphs the same window into the wizard: never a second window.

Invite door paste field (N30, designed): validates the moment a paste lands, with no Continue button. It classifies the paste: a join link, a Cloudflare token, or anything else. The join link's shape is v.<name>.workers.dev/join/<code> (N28), and both the bare and the https:// forms are accepted (N29).
Before a space exists there is no capture, no library and no local recording (U1). There is no .dmg lane in v1 (P17); Homebrew installs beside the install line (N49).
The source view has no backticked scaffold-grade name. The inventory calls it just 'source view' (folded under `landing`), so the fixture uses that literal id.

The mermaid diagram uses underscore names (install_net_drop, install_checksum_fail, install_unsupported_os, install_refused_midtake, first_launch, idle_unprovisioned). The spec's scaffold-grade names are kebab-case, and the fixtures use the kebab forms.

regions.title: the cloud setup wizard
regions.heading: Region 2 — the cloud setup wizard (ratified 2026-07-20; per-screen copy ratified 2026-07-25; N42 additions designed 2026-09-30, awaiting ratification). UX-STATEMACHINE.md lines 385-713.

amendments.summary: When the account already holds a non-shroom Worker named v, the space's pages take the label shroom instead. The name row's fact says it once. This applies to that case only; it is a derived label, not a state.

Reconnect your space now opens the repair mood in Settings → Space. The plan is re-probed and the first broken row is current with its own Region 2 state (token · gate-card · wiring · space-storage-gone · name-changed · token-other-account).

amendments.amends: repair token line draft (“…changed its mind about our token…”)
amendments.summary: Redrafted as “Cloudflare stopped accepting shroom's token — create a fresh one and paste it here. Nothing else needs redoing.”

amendments.amends: N13 (box-1 wording) and the 2026-07-20 invisible post-paste-sweep surfacing

amendments.amends: Region 2 entry arrow 2 (tray menu + Record-routed context line)
